summary: Dorothy Maskell specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. She succeeded William Stede and served as Reader of Pāli at SOAS University of London from 1949 to 1956.

Douglas Allen is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his BA at Yale and PhD at Vanderbilt. He taught at Southern Illinois University and Central Connecticut State before a long career at the University of Maine from 1974.

Douglas Barrett was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied classics at Oxford and attended SOAS University of London. He spent his career at the British Museum, where he was appointed curator from 1969 to 1977.

Douglas Craven Phillott was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and history-archaeology. Educated at Felsted School and Sandhurst, he served as Lecturer in Urdu and Hindustani at Gonville and Caius College and was a Fellow of The Asiatic Society.

Douglas Gildow works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou, later holding posts at Florida State University and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Douglas J. Penick is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Princeton University from circa 1962 to 1966 and trained under traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa in 1971.

Douglas L. Berger works in philosophy, Sinology, and Indology. He taught philosophy at Southern Illinois University Carbondale and later held posts at Leiden University as Professor of Global and Comparative Philosophy and Director of the Centre for Intercultural Philosophy.

Douglas Ober is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history-archaeology. He studied at the University of Washington and earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Harjot Oberoi.

Douglas Osto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Grinnell, Harvard, the University of Washington, and SOAS, where he completed his PhD under Ulrich Pagel before joining Massey University as a Senior Lecturer in 2005.

Douglas Q. Adams is a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Chicago from circa 1967 to 1972 and held a post at the University of Idaho around 1974.

Douglas S. Duckworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology who earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has held teaching posts at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute and East Tennessee State University.
Dragana Majhen is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned a master's degree at the University of Manitoba under the supervision of thesis advisor Albert Welter.

Dragomir Dimitrov specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn, held academic posts there, and served as a Foreign Adjunct Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Dramdul is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as Director of the China Tibetology Research Center and was editor-in-chief of Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region.
Drodul Dorji Tenzin was a religious figure who studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Drodul Pawo Dorje studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught students including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Ayu Khandro, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Drolkar Chungchung studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Drolma is a Tibetologist who completed an M.Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik.
Drubwang Shakya Shri studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

id: P:Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé
summary: Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.
